extracted.intended_audience: linguistics and multimodal humor researchers; graduate students studying humor in comics
extracted.subtask_description: Apply script-based semantic and General Theory of Verbal Humor (GTVH) frameworks to analyze how humor is produced in newspaper comic strips via verbal, visual, or combined multimodal resources. Focus is on political comic strips and identification of script oppositions, logical mechanisms, and knowledge resources that resolve incongruities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mode of humor production (text only / text+image / image only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorize whether humor is produced via verbal medium only, via both verbal and visual media (interaction), or via visual medium only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper classifies comic strips into three categories (text-only, text-and-image interaction, image-only). Definitions: text-only — humor based on language while images provide background/situation; text+image — humor emerging from interaction of the two semiotic modes; image-only — humor produced exclusively by pictorial elements. Empirical counts in this study: 49 text-only, 22 text+image, 3 image-only (out of 74).

rubrics_metrics.name: Script Opposition (SO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the opposed scripts explicitly stated or inferentially understood by readers (the semantic oppositions that generate incongruity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SO is one of the six GTVH Knowledge Resources. Typical script oppositions (Raskin) include normal/abnormal, actual/non-actual, possible/impossible, good/bad, life/death, non-sex/sex, money/non-money, high stature/low stature. Clearly mark the two scripts whose opposition creates the expectation violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical Mechanism (LM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the non-serious/playful logic that resolves the incongruity between opposed scripts (how the joke 'works').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LM explains the mechanism that links scripts (e.g., analogy, metonymy, absurd transfer, exaggeration). The analysis should show how the mechanism allows readers to resolve the incongruity and find a humorous interpretation (e.g., skeleton asking for a beer and a mop — analogy/metonymic replacement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Situation (SI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the background of events (participants, objects, activities, places) that set up the comedic context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SI is a GTVH Knowledge Resource. Document how the depicted situation supports or sets up the script opposition (e.g., bar setting, circus ring, parliamentary setting). Images often supply situational background even when humor is verbal-only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target (TA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the human target(s) of the humor (people, institutions, behaviors, beliefs) that the strip criticizes or jokes about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TA focuses analysis on who or what is being ridiculed or highlighted (e.g., politicians, institutions such as KPK, social practices). Establish whether the target is explicit or implicit and how readers infer it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Strategy (NS) — jab line / punch line / sequencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze text organization and storytelling choices (narratives, dialogues, riddles, puns), including placement of jab lines and punch lines within panels or sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NS (a GTVH KR) includes whether the punch/jab line occurs in the middle or end, whether humor is distributed across panels, and how sequence/timing affects salience. Note where a jab line or punch line is positioned and whether sequences produce cumulative or multi-level effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language (LA) — linguistic resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine linguistic resources (phonological, morphological, syntactic, lexical) exploited to produce humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LA (a GTVH KR) covers devices like homonymy/puns, phonological jokes, semantic shifts. Example from the paper: the pun on 'hak' (heels/rights) that creates the punch line and political critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of SSTH (Script-based Semantic Theory) — identify two opposed scripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply SSTH by locating two opposed scripts whose clash creates the humorous effect (the expectation violation principle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SSTH requires explicit identification of the opposed scripts (e.g., normal vs abnormal actions). Show how violation of expectation (e.g., impossible/possible, real/unreal) produces humor; list which pair of scripts is at work for each example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction type between verbal and visual modes (complementary vs contradictory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify the relationship between text and image as complementary (supporting/enhancing) or contradictory (counterpointing/creating contrast).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complementary interaction: images and text jointly create the same script opposition or enhance meaning. Contradictory interaction: text and image present differing or opposing cues, producing irony or additional incongruities. Analyze degree and distribution of information to determine dynamic (e.g., panels where images imply indifference while text claims concern).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperdetermination / multimodal hyperdetermination
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect cases where multiple humorous readings co-occur (textual hyperdetermination) or where verbal and visual KRs yield different script oppositions producing more than one humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hyperdetermination occurs when one comic yields two or more active, opposed scripts or multiple jab/punch lines (e.g., a pun co-occurring with a visual metaphor). Note when visual and verbal elements generate distinct but concurrent script oppositions and document each.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linguistic devices that produce humor (puns, exaggerations, contradictions, analogies, parallelisms, verbal metaphors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify specific linguistic devices used to create humorous effect in the verbal component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List instances of puns/homonymy, exaggeration, contradiction, analogy, parallelism, and verbal metaphors. Provide examples and show how each device contributes to script opposition and resolution (e.g., exaggeration as a means to criticize political behavior).

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual devices and pictorial resources (panels, body types, facial expressions, pictograms, pictorial runes, visual metaphors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify visual stylistic features that contribute to humor: panel arrangement, gutters, body proportion, posture, expression, balloons, onomatopoeia, pictograms, pictorial runes, and visual metaphors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document how each visual resource creates or supports scripts and logical mechanisms (e.g., animal-symbol metaphors for political figures; facial exaggeration as support for a verbal jab). Note occurrences where images alone produce the punch line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of readers' background knowledge and cultural context
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for the audience's shared knowledge, cultural values, and psychological traits needed to recover implicatures and explicatures in multimodal humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following relevance-theoretic reasoning in the paper, demonstrate which background assumptions are required (e.g., knowledge of local political scandals, conventions of character types, intercultural norms about swearing) and how they resolve incongruities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytic procedure for multimodal humor (three-step method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow a systematic method: (1) classify comic strips by mode of incongruity (text-only, text-image, image-only); (2) identify two opposed scripts via SSTH; (3) observe resolution / logical mechanism using readers' KRs (GTVH).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This methodological rubric prescribes sequence of analysis. Use GTVH's six KRs to document how readers infer humor. The paper models this three-step approach with worked examples (e.g., the skeleton-bar joke; Kompas strips).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequencing and panel-level timing as humor resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat panel arrangement and temporal sequence as resources that shape set-up and punchline timing across single- and multi-panel strips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze how the sequence (single panel vs multiple panels) affects timing, build-up, and distribution of humor (e.g., multi-panel sequences enabling buildup to a punch or producing multiple, levelled jabs). Note how changing panel order or framing can alter script interpretation.
